what: Ares Management invests money for institutions in private credit, private equity, real estate and infrastructure. Private credit, lending directly to companies instead of through banks, is its largest and best-known business.
customers: Pension funds, insurers, sovereign wealth funds and increasingly wealthy individuals investing in its funds.
money: direct lending, liquid credit and alternative credit
secondary fund purchases and wealth products
moat: A twenty-five year lending record that institutions underwrite, and fund structures that lock capital up for years, so fee income is unusually predictable.
risks: Private credit losses would rise in a recession and have not been tested in one at this scale
Net margin of about 9% looks low because consolidated funds inflate revenue
Fundraising slows when institutions are over-allocated to private assets
opportunities: Fee-paying assets under management keep growing, which is what drives earnings
Wealthy individual investors are a large new source of capital
watch: Fee-paying assets under management and fee-related earnings growth.
